answer: Each enrolment seals a new identity inside a walnut whose three-mark label is drawn from a small public dictionary, and any two seats sharing a label are split open into an audit, so a farm's cost tracks the birthday bound rather than its effort. A lone agent's shell almost never repeats; a thousand-identity orchard collides roughly k squared over twice the dictionary size times, and each collision drags the kernel of the hidden seat into the open. The trellis holds only as many names as its lattice keeps apart, and grinding fails because the dealer, not the applicant, assigns the marks.
